analysis.title: Weekly commentary: AI's rising bill of expectations
key_insights: BII downgraded U.S. equities to neutral last month to lock in profits, but says its conviction in AI fundamentals remains intact.
The earnings growth gap has flipped for the first time since 2022: S&P 493 earnings are growing about 29% versus about 18% for the "magnificent seven" (Q3 includes estimates).
Consensus expects S&P 500 earnings to grow about 30% this quarter, a third consecutive quarter above 20% (LSEG data), so the bar for results is high.

Hyperscaler capital spending rose to about $649B over the past year from about $357B in the prior-year period (Bloomberg), leaving little cash surplus after capex. Free cash flow is negative for some firms.
Hyperscaler operating margins edged up to 27.1% from 26.9%, but incremental margins fell to 27.9% from 40.4%, meaning each added dollar of revenue produces less added profit.

Companies with higher AI adoption outside the S&P 500 tech and communication sectors are on track for 3% higher earnings growth this quarter than lower adopters, based on AI mentions in regulatory filings.

Cloud revenue growth at Microsoft and Alphabet points to sustained AI demand, but whether demand justifies the scale of investment is described as an open question, to be debated at BII's 2027 internal Outlook Forum this week.
The AI buildout is increasingly debt-financed. Credit markets are a signpost for how much more AI investment can be financed and at what cost.
BII expects the ebb and flow of AI investment expectations to drive competition for capital and keep bond yields around structurally higher levels. Treasuries rallied alongside the tech sell-off.
The Nasdaq Composite had its worst month since March 2025 as concerns over returns on AI spending intensified.
10-year Treasury yields fell nearly 6 basis points to 4.93% last week after the Fed held rates unchanged, as expected.

BII is selective on AI exposure and favors companies and listed infrastructure that benefit from bottlenecks in the buildout, a key reason for the September move back to EM equities overweight, with the opportunity playing out in Asia.
Recent chipmaker results point to tight supply and strong AI demand. Brazil's post-election selloff bears watching but does not change the EM overweight.
October U.S. payrolls (Nov. 6) are the focus. BII expects stronger wage pressure than in recent jobs reports, which could add to core services inflation.

Positioning: neutral U.S., Europe, UK, Japan and China equities, overweight EM equities. Overweight short-term U.S. Treasuries (expectations of further Fed hikes look excessive), neutral long-term Treasuries, underweight long-term IG credit and Japanese government bonds, overweight EM local currency debt.

sector_views.rationale: Strong AI fundamentals remain supportive and BII continues to favor AI and tech, though scrutiny and near-term volatility are rising.
BII favors these within a neutral Europe stance.
Scarcity, secure supply and power demand carry inflation risks, which these exposures address.

earnings_insights: Consensus expects Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth of about 30% y/y (LSEG), a third straight quarter above 20%. This is an estimate, not a reported figure.
Q3 EPS growth of about 29% for the S&P 493 versus about 18% for the magnificent seven (Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, Tesla). Chart note says Q3 and Q4 figures include estimates.
Hyperscaler operating margin 27.1% versus 26.9% over the prior four quarters, incremental margin 27.9% versus 40.4% (Bloomberg, trailing four quarters, as reported).
Cloud revenue growth at Microsoft and Alphabet cited as evidence of sustained AI demand. No figures given.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Yield fell nearly 6 basis points after the Fed held rates unchanged, as Treasuries rallied alongside the tech sell-off.
The Fed kept rates unchanged, as expected. BII says expectations for further Fed hikes look excessive.
Consensus per LSEG. A high bar for results this season.

macro_indicators.reading: stronger wage pressures than recent reports expected
macro_indicators.interpretation: BII expects firmer wages, which could add to core services inflation. Release is Nov. 6.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight EM equities via AI bottleneck exposure, mainly Asia
trade_ideas.rationale: Strong earnings and cheaper valuations, with chipmaker results pointing to tight supply and strong AI demand.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight short-term U.S. Treasuries, neutral long-term Treasuries
trade_ideas.rationale: Much of the anticipated repricing has occurred and expectations for further Fed hikes look excessive. The front end offers income and a greater breakeven buffer.
trade_ideas.risk: Yields could still rise as competition for capital intensifies.

trade_ideas.rationale: Attractive yield relative to its volatility and improving fundamentals.

risk_factors: Returns on AI capex may not keep pace with spending, with incremental margins falling and free cash flow turning negative for some firms.
Debt-financed AI buildout raises leverage and funding-capacity concerns.
A tight labor market and wage pressure could push up core services inflation.
Policy uncertainty could fuel near-term U.S. equity volatility.
Yields could keep rising as competition for capital intensifies.
Higher energy prices could push euro area rates higher.
charts_described: Bar chart of 2026 year-over-year EPS growth by quarter for the magnificent seven versus the S&P 500 ex-Mag 7. Text states Q3 is roughly 18% versus 29% and Q3 and Q4 include estimates.
vol_and_positioning: BII sees near-term volatility in U.S. equities as AI scrutiny intensifies and policy uncertainty persists, and stays neutral U.S. equities after the downgrade to lock in profits.
BII notes it took EM profits midyear and returned to overweight in September, and stresses staying nimble.
geopolitical: Brazil's post-election selloff, which BII says bears watching but does not change its EM overweight.

tension_points.bull_case: Cloud revenue growth at Microsoft and Alphabet shows sustained AI demand, and higher AI adopters outside tech are on track for 3% higher earnings growth.
tension_points.bear_case: Hyperscaler capex of about $649B leaves little cash surplus, incremental margins fell to 27.9% from 40.4%, and the buildout is increasingly debt-financed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Q3 earnings season results that fail to show returns holding up against the spending, which BII says is key to its medium-term conviction.
